writeup: TIC 60192021 is an eclipsing binary star candidate with an orbital period of 9.8743 days. The primary eclipse produces a 10.46 percent dimming, while a secondary eclipse has been detected at 6.6 sigma significance. Automated analysis of TESS photometry data identified this system with a detection signal-to-noise ratio of 145.2, and pixel-level image analysis confirmed the signal with a peak signal-to-noise of 21.1, though the centroid offset of 3.4 arcsec from the target warrants attention. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a novel find. The machine learning screening score of 0.58 indicates moderate confidence that this represents a genuine target star rather than an instrumental artifact.
